questions.question: A train speeds before a pole in 10 seconds and a platform 150 m long in 20 seconds. Find the length of the train in meters.
questions.explanation:
Let the length of the train be x meters and its speed by y m/sec.

And time =10 second

We know that,

Speed = \(\frac{\text{distance}}{\text{time}}\)

Put the values,

\(y = \frac{x}{10}\)

With platform,new length =x+150m and time =20 sec

By using speed formula ,Them we get

\(\frac{x + 150}{20} = \frac{x}{10}\)

=> 10(x + 150) = 20x

=> 10x + 1500 = 20x

=>20x-10x=1500

=>10x=1500

=>x=150 meters.

Hence, the correct option is 150 meters.

questions.question: A train 175 m long passes a person, running at 4 km/hr in the same direction in which the train is going in 20 seconds. Calculate the speed of the train.
questions.explanation:
Given Information:
• Length of the train is 175 meters.
• Speed of the person is 4 km per hour.
• The person and the train are moving in the same direction.
• Time taken to pass the person completely is 20 seconds.

Calculation:
When a train passes a person, the distance covered is equal to the length of the train.

Distance = 175 meters.

Time = 20 seconds.

So, relative speed = Distance / Time
Relative speed = 175 / 20
Relative speed = 8.75 m per second.

This is the speed of the train relative to the person.
Since both are moving in the same direction, relative speed is equal to the speed of the train minus the speed of the person.

Speed of the person = 4 km per hour
Convert into m per second.

4 × 5 / 18 = 10 / 9 m per second.

Let the speed of the train be x m per second.

Then, x − 10 / 9 = 8.75

8.75 = 35 / 4

So, x − 10 / 9 = 35 / 4

x = 35 / 4 + 10 / 9

Take LCM of 4 and 9 which is 36.

x = (35 × 9 + 10 × 4) / 36
x = (315 + 40) / 36
x = 355 / 36 m per second.

Now convert into km per hour.

Speed in km per hour = 355 / 36 × 18 / 5
Speed in km per hour = 355 / 10
Speed in km per hour = 35.5 km per hour.

So, the speed of the train is 35.5 km per hour.
Hence, option B is correct.

Used Concepts:
• When a train passes a person, the distance covered is equal to the length of the train.
• Relative speed in the same direction is found by subtracting speeds.
• Conversion of km per hour to m per second using multiplication by 5 / 18.
• Conversion of m per second to km per hour using multiplication by 18 / 5.
• Speed = Distance / Time.

questions.question: A train running at the speed of 12 m/s, and passes a platform in 1 minute. It takes 90 seconds to pass a bridge of twice the length of the platform. Find the length of the train.
questions.explanation:
Given Information:
• Speed of the train is 12 meters per second.
• Time taken to pass the platform is 1 minute.
• Time taken to pass the bridge is 90 seconds.
• Length of the bridge is twice the length of the platform.

Calculation:
First convert 1 minute into seconds.

1 minute = 60 seconds.

Let the length of the train be T meters.
Let the length of the platform be P meters.

When the train passes the platform, the distance covered is length of train plus length of platform.

Distance = speed × time
Distance = 12 × 60
Distance = 720 meters.

So,
T + P = 720 ………(1)

The bridge is twice the length of the platform, so its length is 2P meters.

When the train passes the bridge, the distance covered is length of train plus length of bridge.

Distance = speed × time
Distance = 12 × 90
Distance = 1080 meters.

So,
T + 2P = 1080 ………(2)

Now subtract equation (1) from equation (2).

(T + 2P) − (T + P) = 1080 − 720
P = 360 meters.

Now put P = 360 in equation (1).

T + 360 = 720
T = 360 meters.

So, the length of the train is 360 meters.
Hence, option D is correct.

Used Concepts:
• When a train crosses a platform or bridge, distance covered equals length of train plus length of platform or bridge.
• Distance = Speed × Time.
• Formation and solution of linear equations.

questions.question: Two trains of equal length are running on parallel lines in the same direction at 70 km/hr and 46 km/hr. The faster train crossed the slower train in 54 seconds. The length of each train is:
questions.explanation:
Given Information:
• Two trains are of equal length.
• Speed of the faster train is 70 km per hour.
• Speed of the slower train is 46 km per hour.
• Both trains are running in the same direction.
• Time taken to completely cross each other is 54 seconds.

Calculation:
Since both trains are moving in the same direction, we take the difference of their speeds to find the relative speed.

Relative speed = 70 − 46 = 24 km per hour.

Now convert km per hour into m per second.

24 × 5 / 18 = 20 / 3 m per second.

When one train completely crosses the other, the total distance covered is the sum of their lengths.
Let the length of each train be L meters.
So total distance = L + L = 2L.

Distance = Speed × Time
2L = (20 / 3) × 54

2L = 20 × 18
2L = 360

L = 360 / 2
L = 180 meters

So, the length of each train is 180 meters.
Hence, option A is correct.

Used Concepts:
• Relative speed in the same direction is found by subtracting the speeds.
• Conversion of speed from km per hour to m per second using multiplication by 5 / 18.
• Distance = Speed × Time.
• When two trains cross each other, distance covered equals the sum of their lengths.

questions.question: A man travelled a certain distance by train at the rate of 50 kmph and walked back at the rate of 10 kmph. If the whole journey took 6 hours, find the distance.
questions.explanation:
Given Information:
• A man travels a certain distance by train at a speed of 50 km per hour.
• He walks back the same distance at a speed of 10 km per hour.
• Total time taken for the whole journey is 6 hours.
• The distance is the same in both directions.
• We have to find the distance.

Calculation:
Let the distance between the two places be D km.

Time taken to go by train = distance / speed
Time taken = D / 50 hours.

Time taken to walk back = distance / speed
Time taken = D / 10 hours.

According to the question, total time is 6 hours.

So,
D / 50 + D / 10 = 6

Take LCM of 50 and 10 which is 50.

D / 50 + 5D / 50 = 6
6D / 50 = 6

D / 50 = 1
D = 50

So, the distance is 50 km.
Hence, option A is correct.

Used Concepts:
• Time = Distance / Speed.
• When the same distance is travelled at different speeds, separate time expressions are added.
• Formation and solution of a linear equation.

questions.question:
The length of two trains (A and B) is 270 m and 720 m, respectively. If they are going in the same direction, train B takes 55 seconds to pass train A completely and if they are going in opposite directions, they pass each other completely in 9 seconds. Find the speed of train A?

Note: Speed of train B > Speed of train A
questions.explanation:
Given Information:

  • Length of train A = 270 m,
  • length of train B = 720 m.
  • When moving in the same direction, B passes A in 55 sec; when in opposite directions, they cross in 9 sec.
  • Speed of B > Speed of A.

 

Calculation:

Let the speed of train B = x m/s

Speed of the train A = y m/s

ATQ,

x – y = 99055

x – y = 18

x = 18 + y............I

And,

x + y =9909

x + y = 110..............II

From eq. I Put the value of x in eq. II

18 + y + y = 110

18 + 2y = 110

2y = 92,

y = 46

Speed of the train A = 46 m/s

Concept Used:
When trains move in the same direction, relative speed = (Speed of B – Speed of A);
when in opposite directions, relative speed = (Speed of A + Speed of B).

questions.question: Train A having length 450 m crosses a platform thrice of its length in 36 sec. Train B running at the speed of 54 kmph crosses a standing man in 50 sec. Find the time taken by both trains to cross each other when running in the same direction.
questions.explanation:
Speed of train A  = 450+3×45036 =180036=50 m/s

Speed of train B = 54×518=15 m/s

Length of train B = 15×50=750 m

Relative speed when both trains running in the same direction =50 - 15 = 35 m/s

Required time = 450 + 75035=120035=2407=3427 seconds

questions.question: Train P crosses a pole in 4 seconds. Train Q coming from the opposite direction crosses a bogie of train P of length 14 of train P in 2 seconds. The length of Train P and Train Q are in the ratio 7:3. Find the speed of Train P, if the speed of Train Q is 20 m/s.

Speed of train Q =20 m/s

And, the length of trains P and Q is 7k and 3k.

Speed of train P =7k4 m/s.

Length of one bogie of train P =7k4

Relative speed = 7k4+ 20

3k+7k47k4+20=2

19k4=14k4+405k4=40k=32

Speed of train P =7k4 =56 m/s

questions.question: A train can go 150 km in 5 hours but there was an accident midway. After the accident, the speed of the train reduces by 33.33%. If the accident occurs after covering 90 km, then find the total time taken by the train.
questions.explanation:
Speed of train A \(= \frac{150}{5}\  = \ 30\ km/hr\)

Speed of train A after accident \(= \ \frac{2}{3} \times 30 = \ 20\ km/hr\)

Distance covered by train after accident \(= \ 150 - 90\  = \ 60\ km\)

Total Time taken by train \(= \frac{90}{30} + \frac{60}{20} = 6\ hr\)

questions.question: The ratio of lengths of two trains Alfa express and Beeta express is 6:9 and the ratio of the time taken by both trains to cross a man standing on a platform is 3:1. If the speed of Alfa is 30 km/hr, find the speed of Beeta.
questions.explanation:
Let the length of Alfa express and Beeta express be 6x and 9x respectively, and time taken by the both trains to cross the man be 3t and t respectively.

So the speed of first train = \(\frac{6x}{3t} = \frac{2x}{t}\)

Given that,

Speed of Alfa train = 30 km/hr

Therefore,

30 = \(\frac{2x}{t}\)

\(\frac{x}{t} = 15\)…….(i)

Now the speed of train Beeta = \(\frac{9x}{t}\)…….(ii)

Putting the value of \(\frac{x}{t}\) from equation (i) in (ii)

9 x 15 = 135 km/hr

questions.question: A goods train and a passenger train are running on the parallel tracks in the same direction. The driver of the goods train observes that the passenger train coming from behind overtakes and crosses his train completely in \(1\ min\) whereas a passenger on the passenger train marks that he crosses the goods train in \(⅔\ min\). If the speeds of the trains are in the ratio of \(1:2\), then find the ratio of their lengths.
questions.explanation:
let the speeds of the two trains be \(x\) and \(2x\) and length be A and B respectively.

Given, \(A + B\ /\ 2x - x = 1\ min = 60\ s\ \ldots\ldots(1)\)

And \(A\ /\ 2x - x\  = \ ⅔\ min\  = 40\ s\ \ldots.(2)\)

From equation 1 and 2,

\(A + B\ /\ A\  = \ 60/40\)

\(1 + B/A\  = \ 3/2\)

\(B/A = ½\)

\(A:B = 2:1\)

questions.question: Train X of length 300 meter crosses another train Y of length 1/3rd of the length of train X running in opposite direction of train X in p second. Speed of train X is \(\frac{5}{3}\) times of the speed of train Y. Train X can cross a platform of length 200 meter in 20 second. Find the value of p.
questions.explanation:
As we know

Speed = Distance/ Time

Relative speed of two objects when traveling in the same direction = Speed of object A + Speed of object B

Relative speed of two objects when traveling in the opposite direction = Speed of object A - Speed of object B

Distance travelled by train = Length of train + Length of Plateform

Length of train Y =

\(\frac{1}{3}\) × 300 = 100 meter

Speed of train X = \(\frac{200 + 300}{20}\) = 25 m/sec

Speed of train Y = 25 × \(\frac{3}{5}\) = 15 m/sec

p = \(\frac{300 + 100}{25 + 15} = \ 10\) sec

questions.question: A passenger train and a goods train are running in the same direction on parallel railway tracks. If the passenger train now takes three times as long to pass the goods train as when they are running in opposite directions, then what is the ratio of the speed of the passenger train to that of the good train ?
questions.explanation:
let the speed of passenger and goods train be x and y respectively.

Given, \(x + y = 3(x - y)\)

\(x + y = 3x - 3y\)

\(2x = 4y\)

\(x:y = 2:1\)

questions.question: A train 200 metres long overtook a person, who was walking in the same direction at the rate of 18 km/hr and passed him in 10 seconds. Subsequently, it overtook a second person who was also walking in the same direction, and passed him 20 seconds. If the second person was walking at x m/sec, then find the value of x.
questions.explanation:
Let the speed of the train be a m/s.

Speed of 1st person = 18×518 = 5 m/s

Relative speed of train and 1 st person = (a - 5) m/s

Time taken to cross 1st person by the train = 10 sec

200(a-5)=10

a = 25 m/s

Relative speed of train and 2nd person = 25-x m/s

So,Time taken to cross 2nd person = 20

200(25-x) = 20

x = 15 m/s

questions.question: A train 300 metres long overtook a person, who was walking in the same direction at the rate of 36 km/hr and passed him in 20 seconds. Subsequently, it overtook a second person who was also walking in the same direction, and passed him 20 seconds. If the second person was walking at x m/sec, then find the value of x.
questions.explanation:
Let the speed of the train be a m/s.

Speed of 1st person \(= \ 36 \times \frac{5}{18}\  = \ 10\ m/s\)

Relative speed of train and 1 st person \(= \ a - 10\ m/s\)

Time taken to cross 1st person by the train \(= \ 20\ sec\)

\( \frac{300}{a - 10} = 20\)

\( a\  = \ 25\ m/s\)

Relative speed of train and 2nd person\(\  = \ 25 - x\ m/s\)

So,Time taken to cross 2nd person = 20

\( \frac{300}{25- x} = 20\)

\( x\  = \ 10\ m/s\)

questions.question: Two trains ‘A’ and ‘B’ are moving in opposite directions (from Q and P respectively) towards their destinations ‘P’ and ‘Q’, respectively. Train ‘A’ takes 25 hours and train ‘B’ takes 36 hours, to reach their respective destinations after crossing each other. If the speed of train ‘B’ is 150 km/hr, then find the speed of train ‘A’.

questions.question: The distance between the two trains is 150 km and moving in the opposite direction on the same track. The speed of one train is 65 km/hr and the speed of another train is 55 km/hr. A bird starts flying at a speed of 60 km/hr at the location of the faster train. When it reaches the slower train, it turns around and flies in the opposite direction at the same speed. When it reaches the faster train again it turns around and so on. When the train collide, how far has the bird flown (in km)?
questions.explanation:
Given:
Distance between two trains = 150 km
Speed of the first train = 65 km/hr
Speed of the second train = 55 km/hr
Speed of the bird = 60 km/hr
Formula Used:
Time = Distance/Relative Speed
Calculation:

The train are 150 km apart.
Since, trains are moving in opposite direction.
Relative speed = (65+ 55) km/hr =120 km/hr
Therefore, time taken to collide the train = Distance/Relative Speed = (150/120) hr =1.25 hours
The distance covered by the bird in 1.25 hours = 60 × 1.25 = 75 km
